about:
compose@16: covers by the neighbouring token and by embedding class. compose@7-12 covered a pole with the read token
(sets of up to 16 tokens, pairs, triples) and ended the n-gram line; most poles left fire on many read tokens. This round
lets the read token vary and fixes something else instead:
  next    the token right after the read token is in S (at most 8 tokens): the pole anticipates what comes next
  prev    the token right before the read token is in S (at most 8 tokens): any token after S
  class   the read token is in a class of 9-256 tokens the model's input embedding puts together (the tokens nearest the
          centroid of the pole's commonest read tokens), a category rather than a list

  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round16 protocol | select | build | score | report   (same stages and flags as round7.py)

The engine is compose@7's (round7.py): the same event sample, test split, reader and judge (quick-8+8@2), with a placebo.
Tests:
  next, prev   fire: a snippet ending on a token whose next (previous) token is in S; quiet: a snippet ending on the same
               read token whose next (previous) token is not (strata: the read token). A next snippet ends at the read
               token, so the model never sees the next token: the pole has to expect it.
  class        compose@7's word test with T = the class: a token of the class against other tokens of the same frequency
               band and domain.
Selection, per eligible pole not assignment-grade (atlas, after compose@12), with >= 32 sampled activations in >= 8
windows:
  - next, prev: the fewest of the commonest next (previous) tokens over the pole's sample that reach half of it, at most 8,
    each seen at least twice;
  - class: seeds are the read tokens seen at least twice; the class is every token seen >= SEL["class_min_count"] times
    in the corpus with cosine >= tau to the seeds' count-weighted centroid, for the largest tau on a 0.05 grid (0.6 down
    to 0.15) whose class reaches half of the sample; it must hold 9-256 tokens (8 or fewer is a word cover, which
    compose@7-12 had);
  - precision >= SEL["min_precision"]; the pole keeps its best hypothesis by coverage x precision; the best SEL["cap"] are
    tested.
A pole is assignment-grade when its cover held; its coverage is the cover's.

events.doc:
A uniform sample of every pole's strong activations over the parsed and lexed windows (GPU, one pass, all 36 layers).

  python -m bonsai_interp.events.sample run [--limit W] [--out FILE]   # -> data/events/bonsai1.events.npz
  python -m bonsai_interp.events.sample stats                          # CPU: counts per layer

The windows are those the grammar pass parsed (12,000 English windows of the selection split, grammar/parse.py) and those
sweeplib@5 lexed (every code window of the selection split, codesyn/lex.py), so any condition defined on the parse or the lex
can be evaluated at every sampled activation. Activations are read at full window context (1,024 tokens) from position
RULE["min_pos"] on (window starts are an artifact, FINDINGS 2026-10-18).

A strong activation is >= RULE["strong"] (0.3) of the pole's corpus maximum (the scan's), in the pole's sign. Per pole the
pass keeps the K = 64 strong activations with the smallest hash of their (window, position): a bottom-k sample, uniform over
the pole's strong activations and shared between poles (two poles that fire at one position keep it or drop it together,
when both have enough). It also counts every pole's strong activations by domain. Weak poles (corpus max < 0.5) are skipped.

Per pole (layer, sign, neuron): ids (K) int32 = window * 1024 + position (-1 empty), vals (K) float16 = activation / pole max,
count (int64, all strong activations), count_dom (English, code).

condition_doc:
compose@6's condition library: compose@4's (conds2.py, unchanged) plus anticipation conditions: what comes next.

  next1:C, next2:C   compose@3's condition C holds at the token right after the read token, or the one after that

The read snippet ends at the read token, so the model never sees the next token: a pole that fires before C is
anticipating it from the context. The census (docs/CENSUS.md) found prediction-type poles rising with depth (0% in
L0-11 to 34% in L30-35). For mid layers, this asks whether poles track what is about to come rather than what is here.
Test pairs end on the same read token, one followed by C in the corpus and one not.
read: last token, mean over the 3 PREAMBLES (grammar/run.py score, unchanged)
test_split: English windows parsed by the grammar pass (bonsai1.parse.test.npz) and code windows lexed by sweeplib@5 (bonsai1.lex.test.npz)
coverage: the selected hypothesis's share of the pole's sampled strong activations (selection split)
assignment: a pole is assignment-grade when its cover held; its coverage is the cover's
